mainTopic: Why the משנה says 'עלו מבבל'. אביי and רבא on whether עזרא brought the families up. Sources that each group went up, including the חזקה of כהנים who could not prove their lineage.
overview: The גמרא finishes showing that the place of the בית המקדש is higher than the rest of ארץ ישראל. It then brings a פסוק from ירמיהו to show that ארץ ישראל is higher than all other lands, which explains the word 'עלו' in the משנה. Next it asks why the משנה says 'from בבל' and answers that this supports רבי אלעזר: עזרא left בבל pure, like fine flour, before he went up. אביי and רבא then disagree whether the משנה reads 'עלו' (the families went up on their own) or 'העלום' (עזרא brought them up), and the גמרא defends רבא's reading against two challenges. The גמרא then brings sources for the groups in the משנה's list. For חללים, it brings a ברייתא of רבי יוסי about כהנים who could not prove their lineage but kept their חזקה to eat תרומה. The גמרא gives two different answers about what kind of תרומה they ate and what made their חזקה 'great.' It ends by reading a פסוק in עזרא as forbidding both 'קדש' and 'קדשים', a teaching that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of the proof that the Temple's place is higher
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes a פסוק showing that going to the place of the בית המקדש is called 'going up.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Matters of dispute within your gates, and you shall arise and go up.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof it began at the end of the previous amud. The פסוק says people 'go up' to the place הקב״ה chose, so that place is higher than the rest of the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה used the word 'עלו' (went up), so the גמרא is showing that the Torah speaks of places in terms of height. The words 'וקמת ועלית' show that the בית המקדש is higher than the rest of ארץ ישראל. This sets up the next question about ארץ ישראל compared to other lands.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall arise and go up
Matters of dispute (cases brought to the בית דין)

phrases.english: "Matters of dispute within your gates,
phrases.notes: דברים 17:8

phrases.english: and you shall arise and go up"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a derivation begun at the end of the previous amud.
steps.raayaObject: That the place of the בית המקדש is higher than the rest of ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Where do we learn that ארץ ישראל is higher than all lands?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source showing that ארץ ישראל is higher than every other land.
steps.simpleTranslation: But how do we know that ארץ ישראל is higher than all the other lands?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has a source for the בית המקדש being higher. Now it asks for a source that ארץ ישראל itself is higher than other countries.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה speaks of going up from בבל to ארץ ישראל, not to the בית המקדש. So the גמרא needs a separate proof that leaving any other land for ארץ ישראל counts as 'going up.'

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
Higher

phrases.english: But that Eretz Yisrael is higher
than all lands, from where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל גְּבוֹהָה מִכׇּל אֲרָצוֹת מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the בית המקדש compared with the land to the land compared with other lands.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that ארץ ישראל is higher than all other lands.

steps.title: A verse in ירמיהו‎: ה׳ 'brought up' Israel from all lands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק from ירמיהו that says ה׳ will 'bring up' the Jews from the north and from every land.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Therefore, behold, days are coming, says ה׳, when they will no longer say, As ה׳ lives, Who brought up the children of Israel from the land of Egypt, but rather, As ה׳ lives, Who brought up and Who brought the seed of the house of Israel from the northern land and from all the lands where I had driven them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. Coming back to ארץ ישראל from 'all the lands' is described as being 'brought up.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses 'הֶעֱלָה' (brought up) for a return from every land, not only from מצרים. That means ארץ ישראל is higher than all of them. This explains why the משנה says 'עלו' about leaving בבל.

keyTerms.meaning: Brought up
The northern land
I drove them away (exiled them)

steps.whatToRemember: The Torah describes going to ארץ ישראל from anywhere as 'going up.' That is why the משנה says 'עלו מבבל.'

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״לָכֵן הִנֵּה יָמִים בָּאִים נְאֻם ה׳
phrases.english: As it is written: "Therefore, behold, days are coming, says ה׳,
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 23:7–8

phrases.english: when they will no longer say: As ה׳ lives,

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר הֶעֱלָה אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם.
phrases.english: Who brought up the children of Israel from the land of Egypt.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אִם חַי ה׳ אֲשֶׁר הֶעֱלָה
phrases.english: But rather: As ה׳ lives, Who brought up

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲשֶׁר הֵבִיא אֶת זֶרַע בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: and Who brought the seed of the house of Israel
from the northern land
and from all the lands where I had driven them."

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב לָכֵן הִנֵּה יָמִים בָּאִים נְאֻם ה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ירמיהו 23:7–8 calls the return from all lands 'הֶעֱלָה,' so ארץ ישראל is higher than all lands.

steps.title: Why does the משנה say 'from בבל' and not 'to ארץ ישראל'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה stresses where they came from instead of where they arrived.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the משנה specifically say 'they went up from בבל'? Let it say 'they went up to ארץ ישראל'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is bothered by the משנה's wording. If the point is going up to the higher land, it should name ארץ ישראל, not בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the previous steps, the word 'עלו' is about arriving in ארץ ישראל. Mentioning בבל seems unnecessary, so the גמרא suspects that 'from בבל' is teaching something about בבל itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically?
Let it teach

phrases.english: Why specifically does it teach "they went up from Bavel"?
Let it teach "they went up to Eretz Yisrael"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having explained 'עלו,' the גמרא now questions the words 'מבבל.'
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording 'עלו מבבל' in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the point is going up to the higher land, the destination should be named, not the place they left.

steps.title: It supports רבי אלעזר: עזרא cleaned out בבל first
steps.stepSummary: The wording 'from בבל' supports רבי אלעזר, who says עזרא made בבל like pure fine flour before he left.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבי אלעזר, who said: עזרא did not go up from בבל until he made it like clean fine flour, and then he went up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'from בבל' is chosen on purpose. It shows that these families were taken out of בבל, as רבי אלעזר says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר teaches that עזרא took all the families with doubtful יחוס out of בבל, leaving it pure like sifted flour. The משנה's stress on 'from בבל' fits this: the ten groups were removed from בבל, and that is why בבל was left clean.

keyTerms.meaning: It supports him
Clean fine flour (sifted, with no bran)
עזרא the Scribe, who led the return from בבל

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the idea that the Jews who stayed in בבל had especially pure יחוס.

phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Elazar,
for Rabbi Elazar said:
Ezra did not go up from Bavel
until he made it like clean fine flour, and then he went up.
phrases.notes: He means עזרא took out the families with doubtful lineage, so the ones left in בבל were 'clean.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the wording 'מבבל.'
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the wording as deliberate, matching a known אמורא's teaching.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'From בבל' seemed like extra wording; the focus should have been the destination.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'From בבל' teaches that the questionable families were removed from בבל, as רבי אלעזר says.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר: עזרא made בבל like 'סולת נקיה' by taking the questionable families with him.

steps.title: אביי and רבא disagree on the משנה's word
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the משנה reads 'עלו' (they went up on their own); רבא says it reads 'העלום' (he brought them up).
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: אביי said, 'They went up,' meaning on their own, is what we learned. And רבא said, 'He brought them up' is what we learned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a disagreement over the exact wording of the משנה. אביי reads 'עלו,' and רבא reads 'העלום.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two readings say different things. 'עלו' means the families chose to go up. 'העלום' means עזרא took them, even if they did not want to go.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (an argument among אמוראים)
On their own
He brought them up
We learned (in the משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: אביי and רבא are not arguing about the history in general. They are arguing about which word appears in the משנה, and each word has a different meaning.

phrases.english: It was stated: Abaye said:
"They went up," on their own, is what we learned.
And Rava said: "He brought them up" is what we learned.
phrases.notes: In רבא's reading, עזרא is the one doing the bringing, even against their will.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר אַבָּיֵי אָמַר עָלוּ מֵאֵילֵיהֶם תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about the wording of the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: the משנה reads 'עלו' (on their own). רבא: the משנה reads 'העלום' (he brought them up).

steps.title: Their argument depends on רבי אלעזר's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says אביי and רבא disagree about רבי אלעזר's statement and quotes it again.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they disagree about רבי אלעזר's statement, for רבי אלעזר said: עזרא did not go up from בבל until he made it like clean fine flour, and then he went up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its explanation of the argument. It links the two readings to רבי אלעזר and quotes his statement again so we have it in front of us.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to show the reason behind each reading. By pointing to רבי אלעזר, it suggests that the argument is about whether עזרא actively took out the questionable families. The next step spells out who holds what.

keyTerms.meaning: They disagree

phrases.english: And they disagree about Rabbi Elazar's statement,
for Rabbi Elazar said:
Ezra did not go up from Bavel
until he made it like clean fine flour, and then he went up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the two readings in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument between אביי and רבא depends on רבי אלעזר's statement.

steps.title: אביי rejects רבי אלעזר; רבא accepts him
steps.stepSummary: First explanation: אביי does not hold like רבי אלעזר, and רבא does.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי does not hold of רבי אלעזר's view. רבא does hold of רבי אלעזר's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the first way to understand the argument. אביי disagrees with רבי אלעזר, and רבא agrees with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If עזרא did not clean out בבל, the families simply went up on their own, which fits אביי's reading 'עלו.' If עזרא did clean out בבל, he took the families himself, which fits רבא's reading 'העלום.'

keyTerms.meaning: He does not hold (of this view)
He holds (of this view)

phrases.english: Abaye does not hold of Rabbi Elazar's view.
Rava does hold of Rabbi Elazar's view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the connection set up in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First explanation: אביי rejects רבי אלעזר's teaching, and רבא accepts it.

steps.title: Second explanation: both accept רבי אלעזר but disagree about free will
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, both hold like רבי אלעזר. They disagree only on whether the families went up willingly after being separated, or were forced.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say that everyone holds of רבי אלעזר's view, and here they disagree about this. One master holds that עזרא separated them, and they went up on their own. The other master holds that he brought them up against their will.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to explain the argument. Both אביי and רבא agree that עזרא cleaned out בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the argument is narrower. Everyone agrees עזרא separated the questionable families. אביי says they then went up by choice ('עלו'), while רבא says עזרא forced them up ('העלום').

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (another explanation)
Everyone
He separated them
Against their will

steps.whatToRemember: There are two explanations. (1) אביי rejects רבי אלעזר and רבא accepts him. (2) Both accept רבי אלעזר; אביי says the families went up willingly after being separated, and רבא says they were forced.

phrases.english: If you want, say:

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: everyone holds of Rabbi Elazar's view,
and here they disagree about this:
One master holds: he separated them,
phrases.notes: This 'master' is אביי, who reads 'עלו.'

phrases.english: and they went up on their own,
and the other master holds: he brought them up against their will.
phrases.notes: This one is רבא, who reads 'העלום.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second explanation of the argument instead of the one in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both accept רבי אלעזר. אביי: separated, then went up willingly. רבא: brought up against their will.

steps.title: שמואל's statement fits 'they went up' but seems to clash with 'he brought them up'
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's rule that ארץ ישראל is 'dough' compared to בבל makes sense if the families came on their own. If עזרא brought them up after checking them, everyone's lineage was known.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says 'they went up' on their own. That is why שמואל said all lands are mixed compared to ארץ ישראל, and ארץ ישראל is mixed compared to בבל. But for the one who says 'he brought them up,' they knew exactly who everyone was!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's reading, העלום ('he brought them up'). It uses שמואל's statement that the lineage in ארץ ישראל is less clean than in בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If people went up on their own with no checking, mixed lineage in ארץ ישראל is easy to explain. If עזרא picked and checked everyone who came, their lineage should have been fully known. Then ארץ ישראל should not be 'dough' at all.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (opens a 'this view works, but that one doesn't' challenge)
Dough: a mixture, meaning lineage that is mixed and doubtful
They surely knew them (their lineage was known)

phrases.english: It makes sense according to the one who says "they went up,"

phrases.aramaic: הַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: this is what Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
All lands are "dough" compared to Eretz Yisrael,
phrases.notes: "Dough" means mixed up. The lineage there is less certain.

phrases.english: and Eretz Yisrael is "dough" compared to Bavel.
But according to the one who says "he brought them up,"
they certainly knew them!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר: ״עָלוּ״, הַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the two readings from step 6 against a statement of שמואל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If עזרא checked and brought everyone up, their lineage was known. So ארץ ישראל should not be 'dough' compared to בבל, but שמואל says it is.

steps.title: That generation knew, but later generations did not
steps.stepSummary: Lineage was known to the generation that went up. Later generations lost track, so ארץ ישראל became 'dough.'
steps.simpleTranslation: True, they knew for that generation. For later generations they did not know.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the reading העלום. The checking only helped the people living then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עזרא's checking made lineage clear at the time. Later generations no longer had that clear knowledge, and things got mixed. So שמואל's statement works even if עזרא brought them up.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / true (concedes a point before limiting it)
Generation

phrases.english: Granted that they knew for that generation,
for other generations they did not know.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope (time frame) of the knowledge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since עזרא checked everyone, lineage in ארץ ישראל should be clear forever.
steps.terutzMaskana: The checking helped only that generation. Later generations lost track, so ארץ ישראל can still be called 'dough.'

steps.title: עזרא checking the people at the river seems unnecessary if they were already checked
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says עזרא gathered the people at the river and checked them. That fits 'they went up.' If he brought them up, they had already been checked.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says 'they went up.' That is why the פסוק says: 'I gathered them to the river that goes to Ahava, we camped there three days, and I looked over the people and the כהנים, and I did not find any לוים there.' But for the one who says 'he brought them up,' they had already been careful!
steps.whatsHappening: A second challenge to the reading העלום, this time from a פסוק in עזרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If people came on their own, עזרא had to stop and check who was there. That is exactly what the פסוק describes. If he had picked and checked everyone before leaving, why would he need to check again at the river?

keyTerms.meaning: אחוה: the river where עזרא gathered the people
And I looked closely / examined
They were certainly careful

phrases.english: It makes sense according to the one who says "they went up,"
this is what is written:
"And I gathered them to the river that goes to Ahava,
phrases.notes: עזרא 8:15

phrases.english: and we camped there three days,
and I looked over the people and the priests,
and of the sons of Levi I found none there."
But according to the one who says "he brought them up,"
they were already careful!
phrases.notes: He means they had already checked everyone before leaving, so why check again at the river?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to the reading העלום, using the same 'בשלמא' pattern as step 10.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק shows עזרא checking the people at the river. That would be pointless if everyone had already been checked before leaving.

steps.title: They checked for unfit people, not for proper families
steps.stepSummary: The earlier checking was only about people with a lineage problem. Proper families like לוים were not sorted out until the river.
steps.simpleTranslation: True, they were careful about the unfit. About the fit, they were not careful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends העלום by saying the first checking only removed people with a lineage problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before leaving, they made sure no פסולים came along. They did not sort out who among the proper families was a כהן or a לוי. That is what עזרא did at the river, and why he noticed no לוים were there.

keyTerms.meaning: People with a lineage problem (unfit for marriage into proper families)
People of proper lineage

steps.whatToRemember: Both challenges to העלום are answered. The checking helped only that generation, and it covered only the פסולים. So both readings of the משנה still stand.

phrases.english: Granted that they were careful with the unfit,
with the fit they were not careful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of what was checked
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone was fully checked before leaving, so the checking at the river was pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the פסולים were checked beforehand. The proper families, such as לוים, were sorted out at the river.

steps.title: Where do we know that כהנים, לוים and ישראלים went up?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's list of families and asks for a source that כהנים, לוים and ישראלים went up from בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Priests, Levites and Israelites.' How do we know that they went up?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new part. It quotes the first items in the משנה's list and asks for a source that these groups went up. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed ten family groups that went up from בבל. Now the גמרא wants a פסוק showing that each group really came, starting with כהנים, לוים and ישראלים.

keyTerms.meaning: Priests, Levites and Israelites: the first groups in the משנה's list
From where do we know?
That they went up

phrases.english: Priests, Levites and Israelites.
phrases.notes: These are words quoted from the משנה's list of families that went up.

phrases.english: From where do we know that they went up?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the עלו/העלום discussion and returns to the משנה's list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A scriptural source that כהנים, לוים and ישראלים went up from בבל.

steps.title: A פסוק in עזרא lists כהנים, לוים and all ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק in עזרא says the כהנים, לוים and all of ישראל settled in their cities. That shows they came up.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'The priests, the Levites, some of the people, the singers, the gatekeepers and the נתינים settled in their cities, and all Israel in their cities.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that names these groups among those who settled in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes the people who returned from בבל settling in their cities. It names the כהנים, the לוים and 'all Israel.' So all three groups went up.

keyTerms.meaning: Singers (in the בית המקדש)
Gatekeepers
Gibeonite descendants given to serve the Temple

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And the priests and the Levites settled,
phrases.notes: עזרא 2:70

phrases.english: and some of the people, and the singers,
and the gatekeepers and the Gibeonites, in their cities,
and all Israel in their cities."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עזרא 2:70 names the כהנים, the לוים and all ישראל among those who settled after returning, so all three groups went up.

steps.title: Where do we see that חללים went up?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה's list and asks for a source that חללים went up from בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said חללים, converts and freed slaves went up. How do we know that חללים went up?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next names on the משנה's list and asks for a source about חללים. This sets up the next step, which brings a ברייתא as the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 14 the גמרא asked for a source about כהנים, לוים and ישראלים. Now it does the same for חללים. The point is to show from a text that this group also came up with עזרא.

keyTerms.meaning: Children of a כהן from a marriage the Torah forbids to him. They lose the status of כהונה.
Converts
Freed slaves
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: Ḥalalim, converts and freed slaves.
Ḥalalim: from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same source-request pattern as Step 14, now for the next item on the משנה's list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that חללים went up from בבל to ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: רבי יוסי brings the פסוק about כהנים with no records
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי, who says חזקה is great. He brings the פסוק in עזרא about families of כהנים who could not prove their lineage and were kept away from the most holy offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches, רבי יוסי says: חזקה is great. The פסוק says that some families of כהנים searched for their family records and could not find them. So they were pushed out of כהונה, and they were told not to eat the most holy offerings until a כהן arises with the אורים ותומים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. It quotes a פסוק about כהנים who came up with עזרא but could not prove they were proper כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These families might really have been חללים, since nobody could confirm their lineage. Because the פסוק says they came up and were 'put out from the כהונה,' we see that possible חללים were among the people who came up. רבי יוסי's opening words, 'great is חזקה,' are explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא teaches
Presumptive status: we keep treating someone the way he was treated until now.
A title for the leader who gave the order in the פסוק
The breastplate of the כהן גדול, which could give answers on questions like these

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי says 'great is חזקה' even though these כהנים were pushed out. Do not read 'put out' as losing everything. The next step shows they kept part of their status.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
Great is presumptive status,
as it is said:
"And of the sons of the priests: the sons of Chavayah,
the sons of Hakotz, the sons of Barzillai,

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר לָקַח מִבְּנוֹת בַּרְזִלַּי הַגִּלְעָדִי אִשָּׁה
phrases.english: who took a wife from the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite
and was called by their name.
These searched for their family records
but they were not found,
so they were put out of the priesthood as unfit.
And the Tirshata said to them
that they should not eat of the most holy offerings
until a priest arises with the Urim and Tumim."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: גְּדוֹלָה חֲזָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16 with a ברייתא and a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in עזרא tells of כהנים who could not prove their lineage. They were possible חללים, and they came up from בבל.

steps.title: They keep their חזקה for gifts eaten outside ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. They were told they stay in their חזקה, so they may eat the same gifts in ארץ ישראל that they ate in exile.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: You stay in your חזקה. What did you eat in exile? Only holy gifts that may be eaten anywhere. Here too, you may eat those same gifts.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by explaining how these doubtful כהנים were treated after they came up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They lost the right to eat the most holy offerings, which must be eaten in ירושלים. They kept what they already had in exile, the gifts that may be eaten anywhere, such as תרומה. This is the 'great' power of חזקה: the doubt did not take away their old status.

keyTerms.meaning: The exile, meaning בבל
Holy gifts that may be eaten anywhere, not only in ירושלים, such as תרומה
In your presumptive status

phrases.english: And he said to them:
You remain in your presumptive status.
What did you eat in exile?
The holy gifts of the outlying areas.
phrases.notes: These are gifts like תרומה that may be eaten anywhere, unlike offerings that must stay in ירושלים.

phrases.english: Here too, the holy gifts of the outlying areas.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in Step 17 by spelling out what these כהנים could still eat.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Doubtful כהנים keep their חזקה for gifts eaten anywhere, but they may not eat the most holy offerings.

steps.title: Eating תרומה could lead to full status
steps.stepSummary: Some hold that seeing a person eat תרומה is enough to treat him as a full כהן. If so, letting these doubtful כהנים eat תרומה should lead people to raise them to full status.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a view that we raise someone to full family status because we saw him eat תרומה. According to that view, these people who are eating תרומה will end up being raised to full כהונה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's ruling from the view that eating תרומה proves someone is a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If eating תרומה works as proof of lineage, then the permission to eat תרומה would cause trouble. People would see these doubtful כהנים eating it and treat them as full כהנים, even for marriage and for the most holy offerings. That defeats the limit the פסוק set.

keyTerms.meaning: We raise, meaning we grant someone a status
The gift given to the כהן from produce; only a כהן may eat it
Lineage, family status

phrases.english: And according to the one who says:
We raise someone from תרומה to lineage?
phrases.notes: He means: if we see someone eating תרומה, we treat him as a full כהן.

phrases.english: These who eat תרומה
will come to be raised up!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the permission in Step 18 to eat קדשי הגבול.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that the doubtful כהנים may eat תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If eating תרומה proves lineage, these doubtful כהנים will wrongly be raised to full כהונה.

steps.title: Their status was already known to be weak
steps.stepSummary: The case is different because everyone knew their חזקה was weak, so nobody would be fooled.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because their status was weakened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that these כהנים are a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that eating תרומה raises someone works only when nobody has a reason to doubt him. Here everyone knew about the doubt, since these כהנים did not eat the offerings the other כהנים ate. So seeing them eat תרומה proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there
Weakened, damaged

phrases.english: It is different there,
because their presumptive status was weakened.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Eating תרומה always leads people to treat someone as a full כהן.
steps.terutzMaskana: When everyone already knows a person's status is in doubt, his eating תרומה does not raise him.

steps.title: So what was great about their חזקה?
steps.stepSummary: If their חזקה was weak and gave them only what they already had, what did רבי יוסי mean by 'great is חזקה'?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then what does 'great is חזקה' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי יוסי's opening words and asks what they add.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said their חזקה was weakened. They also gained nothing new, since they ate only gifts like תרומה, just as they had in exile. So it is hard to see why רבי יוסי praises the power of חזקה here.

keyTerms.meaning: But then what is...?

phrases.english: But then what is "great is presumptive status"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 20's answer to question the wording of רבי יוסי in Step 17.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their weak חזקה gave them nothing beyond what they had in exile, so it does not look 'great.'

steps.title: From rabbinic תרומה to Torah תרומה
steps.stepSummary: Their חזקה was great because it moved them from eating rabbinic תרומה in בבל to eating Torah-level תרומה in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first they ate תרומה that was only from the רבנן, and in the end they ate תרומה from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what these כהנים gained from their חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In בבל the תרומה they ate was only a rabbinic obligation. In ארץ ישראל תרומה is from the Torah and is much stricter. Their חזקה was strong enough to let even doubtful כהנים eat it, and that is why it is called 'great.'

keyTerms.meaning: At first
From the רבנן, a rabbinic law
From the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא proves that possible חללים went up with עזרא. In this first answer, their חזקה let them eat Torah-level תרומה in ארץ ישראל, and they were not raised to full כהונה because everyone knew about the doubt. The next step gives a second answer that disagrees.

phrases.english: That at first they ate rabbinic תרומה,
and in the end they ate Torah-level תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Their חזקה gave them nothing new.
steps.terutzMaskana: Their חזקה moved them up from rabbinic תרומה to Torah תרומה.

steps.title: A second answer: they ate only rabbinic תרומה, and that never proves lineage
steps.stepSummary: Even in ארץ ישראל they ate only rabbinic תרומה. Only eating Torah-level תרומה is used to raise someone to full יוחסין, so nobody would be misled.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you could say: even now, in ארץ ישראל, they ate only rabbinic תרומה, not Torah-level תרומה. When we raise a person to full lineage because we saw him eat תרומה, that is only Torah-level תרומה. Rabbinic תרומה does not raise anyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the problem from Step 19: why we were not afraid that people would treat these doubtful כהנים as full כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said everyone knew their חזקה was weak. This answer is different: they only ate rabbinic תרומה, and seeing someone eat rabbinic תרומה never proves he is a real כהן. So there is nothing that could fool anyone.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say: this introduces a second, different answer
Rabbinic level, made obligatory by the חכמים
Torah level, obligatory from the Torah itself
We raise someone to full lineage status

steps.confusionAlert: This answer takes back what Step 22 said. Step 22 said they now ate Torah-level תרומה. This answer says they still ate only rabbinic תרומה even in ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
Really, now too,
phrases.notes: 'Now' means after they came back to ארץ ישראל, just like it was in בבל.

phrases.english: they ate of rabbinic [תרומה],
but of Torah-level [תרומה] they did not eat,
and when we raise someone from תרומה to full lineage,
that is from Torah-level [תרומה];
from rabbinic [תרומה] we do not raise him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the קשיא of Step 19, different from the answer of Steps 20 and 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the rule: only eating Torah-level תרומה proves lineage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Letting them eat any תרומה would lead people to treat them as full כהנים
steps.terutzMaskana: They ate only rabbinic תרומה, which never proves lineage, so there was no danger

steps.title: Then what was great about their חזקה?
steps.stepSummary: If they ate only rabbinic תרומה in ארץ ישראל, just like in בבל, the חזקה gave them nothing new. So why call it great?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does 'great is חזקה' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question as Step 21 again, now against the new answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this new answer, nothing changed when they moved from בבל to ארץ ישראל. So the praise 'great is חזקה' from רבי יוסי seems to have no point.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: if your answer is true
Great is חזקה, the words of רבי יוסי in the ברייתא

phrases.english: If so,
what is meant by 'great is חזקה'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: The words 'great is חזקה' in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the חזקה gave them nothing more than they already had, there is nothing great about it

steps.title: Their חזקה held even when there was a new reason for a גזירה
steps.stepSummary: In בבל there was no Torah-level תרומה, so there was no reason to forbid rabbinic תרומה. In ארץ ישראל there was a reason, but their חזקה still let them eat rabbinic תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first, in בבל, there was no reason to make a גזירה because of Torah-level תרומה. In the end, in ארץ ישראל, even though there was a reason to make a גזירה because of Torah-level תרומה, they still ate rabbinic תרומה. They did not eat Torah-level תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the חזקה was 'great' under the new answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ארץ ישראל there was real Torah-level תרומה around. So the חכמים had a reason to forbid them even rabbinic תרומה, so they would not come to eat the Torah-level kind. The חזקה was strong enough that no such גזירה was made, and that is its greatness.

keyTerms.meaning: At first, here meaning in בבל
To make a גזירה, a rabbinic protective ban
In the end, here meaning in ארץ ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: Second approach: they ate only rabbinic תרומה. The חזקה was 'great' because it held firm even when there was a new reason to stop them.

phrases.english: That at first there was no reason to make a ban
phrases.notes: 'At first' means in בבל, where there was no Torah-level תרומה at all.

phrases.english: because of Torah-level תרומה;

phrases.aramaic: לְבַסּוֹף – אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיכָּא לְמִיגְזַר
phrases.english: in the end, even though there was reason to make a ban
because of Torah-level תרומה,
they ate of rabbinic [תרומה],
of Torah-level [תרומה] they did not eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what made the חזקה great
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חזקה gave them nothing new, so it is not great
steps.terutzMaskana: The חזקה was great because it stopped a גזירה that would otherwise have been made in ארץ ישראל

steps.title: The פסוק in עזרא seems to forbid only the holiest offerings
steps.stepSummary: The התרשתא told them not to eat 'קדש הקדשים.' That sounds like only the holiest offerings were forbidden, so they could eat everything else, even Torah-level תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'And the התרשתא said to them that they should not eat of קדש הקדשים.' So only קדש הקדשים they may not eat, but anything else they may eat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 23 using a פסוק in עזרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names only one forbidden thing: the holiest offerings. If only that was forbidden, they should be allowed to eat Torah-level תרומה. That goes against the claim that they ate only rabbinic תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written: brings a פסוק as a challenge
The governor who led the returning exiles
Holy of holies; here, the holiest kind of offerings

phrases.english: But it is written: 'And the governor said to them'
phrases.notes: עזרא 2:63

phrases.english: 'that they should not eat of the most holy things';
so it is of the most holy things that they may not eat,
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is the corrected wording, making it plural: 'they.'

phrases.english: but anything else they may eat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim of Steps 23 and 25 that they did not eat Torah-level תרומה
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that they ate only rabbinic תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק forbids only the holiest offerings, so it suggests they were allowed even Torah-level תרומה

steps.title: The פסוק forbids two things: 'קדש' and 'קדשים'
steps.stepSummary: The words 'קדש הקדשים' are read as two separate items: anything called 'קדש' and anything called 'קדשים.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he is saying: not anything that is called 'קדש,' and not anything that is called 'קדשים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the פסוק differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase does not mean only 'the holiest offerings.' It is split into two words, each naming a separate group of holy food. Both groups are forbidden, so Torah-level תרומה is included.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he is saying: a re-reading of the words
That is called

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
not anything that is called 'holy,'
and not anything that is called 'holy things.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 26
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reads the פסוק as listing two separate items
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'קדש הקדשים' means only the holiest offerings
steps.terutzMaskana: 'קדש' and 'קדשים' are two separate forbidden groups

steps.title: Sources: 'קדש' means תרומה, 'קדשים' means offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the Torah calls תרומה 'קדש' and calls the parts of offerings 'קדשים,' and begins quoting a teaching on the second פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Not anything called קדש': as it is written, 'No stranger may eat קדש.' 'And not anything called קדשים': as the פסוק says, 'And a כהן's daughter, if she marries a stranger, she may not eat of the תרומה of the קדשים.' And the Master said: 'Of what is set apart from the קדשים...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings פסוקים to prove what each of the two words means. The last line starts a teaching that continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'no stranger may eat קדש' is about תרומה, so 'קדש' means תרומה. The פסוק about the כהן's daughter shows that 'קדשים' means the parts taken from offerings. So the doubtful כהנים were forbidden both Torah-level תרומה and offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: A stranger: someone who is not a כהן
The daughter of a כהן
What is set apart: the parts lifted from an offering for the כהן
The Master said: quotes an earlier teaching

phrases.english: 'Not anything that is called holy':
as it is written: 'No stranger may eat of the holy,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:10

phrases.english: 'and not anything that is called holy things':

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר קְרָא ״וּבַת כֹּהֵן כִּי תִהְיֶה לְאִישׁ זָר
phrases.english: as the פסוק says: 'And a כהן's daughter, if she is married to a stranger,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:12

phrases.english: 'she may not eat of what is set apart from the holy things,'
and the Master said:
'Of what is set apart from the holy things'
phrases.notes: The sentence stops here. The teaching continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings sources to back up the two-word reading of Step 27
steps.raayaObject: That 'קדש' means תרומה and 'קדשים' means parts of offerings
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 22:10 and ויקרא 22:12, with a teaching of the Master
